title: Cloud platform decision
transcript:
Platform Engineering Lead: I've been thinking about the various options for our infrastructure expansion and I've got some concerns, particularly around the loss of control and flexibility if we don't build our own data centers.

CTO: I understand your concerns, but we need to consider the immediate needs of the business as well. We've been given a cost review deadline, and building our own data centers would take 18 months, which is too long.

Finance Partner: Exactly. We can't afford to wait that long when we're under pressure to reduce costs.

SRE: And let's not forget the significant re-architecting required for Google Cloud's Anthos. That's a lot of work and potential disruption.

Platform Engineering Lead: True, but Azure Stack HCI doesn't offer seamless integration with our existing AWS services, leading to potential operational inefficiencies.

SRE: I agree, and AWS Outposts could be a good solution. It allows us to leverage our existing AWS services and maintain control over the hardware.

CTO: Plus, it's immediately available with a quick deployment timeline. And the upfront costs are lower compared to building our own data centers.

Finance Partner: But we need to be aware of potential long-run maintenance costs and vendor lock-in risks.

Platform Engineering Lead: I'll make sure to include a detailed analysis of those factors in my report.

(Off-topic exchange)

Platform Engineering Lead: By the way, have you seen the new Star Wars movie? I heard it's fantastic.

CTO: I haven't had a chance yet, but I'll definitely check it out.

(End of off-topic exchange)

SRE: So, to summarize, we're looking at a provisional decision to lease AWS Outposts for immediate time-to-value.

CTO: Yes, that seems like the best option given the constraints we're working with. I'll sign off on it.

SRE: The SRE team will own the implementation, and I'll ensure to include the caveats and open risks in my report.
document:
Title: AWS Outposts Decision Summary

The team has provisionally decided to lease AWS Outposts for immediate time-to-value. This choice allows us to capitalize on our current AWS service integrations while maintaining control over the hardware. The SRE team will be responsible for the implementation.

The decision was made considering the immediate availability of infrastructure, lower upfront costs compared to building our own data centers, and the seamless integration with existing AWS services. However, a detailed analysis of long-run maintenance costs and potential vendor lock-in risks is pending, as well as an assessment of any potential loss of control or flexibility.

CTO input was sought throughout the discussion.
